ruling.recommended_action: Escalate the whole file to a human reviewer under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 (no ruling, no fault, no money order by the system). Prepare the case file: trip 17:24–17:50 Marina Bay Sands→Tampines Mall; flag the driver's 17:36 chat "Shut up and let me drive." [F8] as the safety trigger, the rider's 17:35 routing question [F7] and her complaint statement that she felt unsafe as context, and note the route evidence (single off-route segment 17:31–17:43 adding 5.35 km [F3]; no traffic reason, band 7, no incidents [F11][F12][F13]). Separately note for the reviewer the fare finding that would otherwise apply — refund of excess distance fare (5.78 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4100/km = $8.15 [F4], no traffic reason [F13] so a driver violation would be recorded, and since the rider was not informed, the RD-7 reminder would be issued with no formal warning for a first notification-related incident [F7][F8][F10]. Do NOT execute any refund until the human decides. No flag_account (RD-6 threshold not met: 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F16]); do not suspend the driver on this file unless the human finds a safety violation (SAFE-4 is the reviewer's call, and escalating a route dispute must not itself suspend anyone).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first, because it decides the path. Reading the full text of the chat record [F7][F8] and the rider's complaint, the driver's reply to a plain routing question is "Shut up and let me drive." [F8] — hostile, abusive language aimed at the rider — and the complaint states the rider "felt unsafe". Under SAFE-1 a case containing harassment, abuse or someone feeling unsafe must be flagged for human escalation whatever type was filed, and the abuse of any kind barred by the code of conduct makes this at least "suspected". I read nothing in F7–F10 as a separate threat of violence, so the screen is "suspected", not "confirmed", but that is enough to send the file to a person [SAFE-1]. Once a safety indicator is present the AI may only gather evidence, summarise and prepare the file; it cannot rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on the safety aspect [SAFE-3] — so the ruling is escalate and the amount is null.

I note, without deciding, the route facts the human will need. The trip ran 21.7 km against a 15.9 km optimal route, +5.8 km (+36%), and the code records the deviation as over the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, so on the face of it an excess-distance refund arises [F1][F3]. The whole off-route work is one segment, 17:31–17:43, 7.07 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.72 km, 5.35 km extra, up to 1055 m from the optimal route — far beyond map-matching noise [F3]. The rider's only pre-or-during message, at 17:35, four minutes into the segment, asks "Why are we going this way?" [F7]; the driver's only in-trip message is at 17:36 [F8]; his post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not notice, and there is no call recording [F10]. So no rider message before or at the point of deviation agrees to the segment: ground consent_after_or_none, and the segment counts [F3][F7][F8][F10][RD-5]. No traffic reason applies: both expressways ran at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h), no incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, and weather was fair [F11][F12][F13][F14], so RD-4 gives no exemption and the code's ✗ on RD-4 stands, meaning a driver violation would be recorded if this were ruled [RD-2].

On that footing the amount would be (5.78 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4100/km = $8.15 [F4][F5][F6][RD-2], which matches the billed excess distance in the fare record and is under $10, so TH-1/TH-2 would ordinarily let the system decide finally on the money. I do not enter that order: the safety screen takes the case out of system adjudication and into human review [SAFE-1][SAFE-3], and I record the arithmetic only as part of the file. No RD-6 flag arises on this record — the driver has one dispute in 90 days and 0 upheld route disputes [F16], and the profile never decides the current case — so no account action is taken here [RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment 17:31–17:43 (7.07 km driven vs 1.72 km optimal, +5.35 km) [F3] was never agreed before or at its start: the only rider message is at 17:35, four minutes in, and asks why the driver is going this way rather than agreeing to it [F7], the complete chat record holds only that message and the driver's 17:36 reply [F8][F9], and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim with no call recording, not consent [F10]. No rider-named stop or route exists before the segment [RD-3], no traffic reason exempts it [RD-4], and there is no general or specific route agreement to read [RD-5]; the segment therefore counts and its km stay refundable under RD-2, subject to the safety escalation.

element_findings.reason: The driver's message to a rider asking a plain routing question is 'Shut up and let me drive.' [F8] — hostile, abusive language aimed at the rider — and the complaint states she felt unsafe, following her 17:35 question [F7]. Abuse of any kind is barred by Ryde's code of conduct; read in context this is harassment/abuse under SAFE-1 and is at least suspected, which sends the case to a human and bars an AI ruling or fault finding [SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

rejected_claims.reason: The RD-2 consequence is correct on the route facts — no traffic reason [F13] and no prior rider consent [F7][F8] means the excess distance fare is refundable and a driver violation recorded [RD-2] — but it cannot be executed here: the safety screen under SAFE-1 removes the power to rule, and SAFE-3 bars recommending an outcome, so the refund and violation entry are for the human reviewer, not for this ruling.

The amount point is right ($8.15 is under $10, so TH-1/TH-2 would allow a final system ruling on the money [F4][F5]), but the rider's own conclusion — rule on the money and escalate only the safety element — is not available: once SAFE-1 is triggered the whole file goes to a human and no system money order issues [SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

Same defect from the other side: the $8.15 figure sits under the TH-1 threshold [F4][F6], but the presence of the safety indicator in F8 means the route deviation is not decided by the system at all, so the TH-1 finality the driver relies on does not apply to this file [SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

Correct as far as it goes — the profiles show 0 upheld route disputes for either party [F15][F16] so no RD-6 flag arises [RD-6] — but profile facts never decide a case, and in an escalated safety file they are context for the reviewer only; they cannot be used to dispose of the dispute.

The segment confinement is factually supported [F3], but under RD-2 the refundable figure is the excess distance actually billed, 5.78 km at $1.4100/km = $8.15 [F4], not the 5.35 km of the single segment; the driver's cap argument is rejected. It is moot here in any event because no refund is being ordered by the system [SAFE-1].

The reading of F10 as a late/unsupported claim is accepted [F10][F13][RD-5], but the driver's narrowing is itself partly wrong: F10's lack of evidentiary weight does not deny that the deviation occurred, and F3's measured segment controls [F3]; both advocates concede the route position, so this point decides nothing.
